title: Rural Data Centers Are in for a Big Federal Tax Break
key_facts: From 1 Jan, rural projects become eligible for corporate tax benefits under the opportunity-zone program expanded by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
Searchlight Institute research, reviewed exclusively by WIRED, found more than 100 data centers in development in eligible rural areas, from a conservative database of under 700 projects.
Pew: 13% of operating data centers are rural but about 67% of planned ones are.
Microsoft and Amazon told WIRED they do not use the program (WIRED says Meta also denied); Google did not respond.
The government estimates the rural expansion will cost $40.9 billion over the next decade; benefits require capital investment, not jobs.
Senator Josh Hawley has introduced a bill to end opportunity-zone funding for data centers.
quote_evidence: Starting next year, projects sited in tracts of rural land across the country will be newly eligible for a set of specific corporate tax benefits under a program expanded by the bill.
WIRED exclusively reviewed the research compiled by Searchlight and found more than 100 data centers under various stages of development in rural areas that could be eligible.
There is no requirement for projects getting opportunity zone benefits to create jobs; the assumption is that they will do so, simply by siting in the community itself.
why_it_matters_hint: A federal tax break could pull data centers to rural areas while states pull back their own incentives.
notes: Weekly WIRED column (Power Play) built on Searchlight research; the tax data is confidential, so actual use is unknown.
